details:
The Problem

Humanity's exploration of the Moon and Mars has left behind an extraordinary collection of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and mission hardware.

Although these machines played important roles in scientific discovery and engineering progress, their stories are often scattered across technical archives, historical documents, and mission websites.

For young space enthusiasts, discovering these stories can be difficult. Technical information alone does not always communicate the excitement, challenges, and human ingenuity behind space exploration.

My Solution: Space Museum

Space Museum is an interactive digital museum designed to turn NASA's historical mission information into an immersive educational journey.

Instead of presenting visitors with a conventional collection of text and photographs, the project combines 3D environments, interactive exhibits, historical storytelling, and robotic characters.

Key Features

1. Interactive 3D Space Museum

Visitors can enter a virtual museum featuring a central atrium and themed exhibition areas, where visitors can freely to move around and explore the museum.

2. Nine Historical Space Exploration Exhibits

The museum features nine lunar and Martian exploration artifacts:

  • Luna 2 Impactor
  • Surveyor 3 Lander
  • Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle Descent Stage
  • Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1)
  • Sojourner Rover
  • Spirit Rover
  • Opportunity Rover
  • InSight Lander
  • Perseverance Discarded Entry, Descent and Landing Hardware

Each exhibit presents mission history, objectives, achievements, engineering details, mission dates, location information, and historical context.

3. Interactive Mission Storytelling

Each exhibit features a five-stage discovery experience:

  • Encounter: Discover the artifact and its historical background.
  • Voice: Hear the spacecraft character tell its story through creative first-person narration.
  • Story Film: Explore an animated visual reconstruction of the mission.
  • Inspect 3D: Examine spacecraft components through interactive 3D hotspots.
  • Facts: Explore mission dates, achievements, technical details, and references.

4. Lumi — The Robotic Museum Guide

Lumi is the museum's robotic guide. It is implemented as a procedural 3D character inside the Three.js environment.

Lumi can patrol the museum, greet visitors, turn toward them, and provide contextual guidance through an interactive guide interface.

5. Mission Timeline and Historical Archive

Visitors can explore the chronological development of lunar and Martian exploration, browse the exhibit archive, and discover the connections between different missions.

6. NASA Archival Resources

The museum integrates NASA mission records, archival photographs, historical references, and selected 3D models to connect the interactive experience with documented space exploration history.

Educational Impact

Space Museum aims to make space science more approachable for school-age students and young enthusiasts.

By combining immersive environments with storytelling and interactive discovery, the project encourages visitors to explore the science and engineering behind historical missions.

We want every visitor to understand that even when a spacecraft stops operating, its contribution to science and exploration continues.

Final Vision

Abandoned but not forgotten.
